original_question: Jutila proved a Weyl-strength twelfth-moment bound for Hecke-Maass cusp forms of level 1 with spectral parameter at most T. Prove a level-aspect analogue in which one sums over Hecke-Maass cusp forms of level q and bounded spectral parameter.
target_in_paper: Problem (13) in the subsection "Moments of the Riemann zeta function": the request for a level-aspect analogue of Jutila’s Weyl-strength twelfth-moment bound for central values of Hecke–Maass cusp forms.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact target in the paper: Problem (13), not the neighboring Problems (12) or (14). It keeps the right object (Hecke–Maass cusp forms), the right known result of Jutila at level 1, the right moment order (twelfth), and the intended change of aspect from the spectral parameter bound t_f ≤ T to varying level q with bounded spectral parameter.
missing_details: The paper’s displayed bound is not just a generic twelfth moment statement; it is specifically Σ_{t_f≤T} L(1/2,f)^12 / L(1,ad f) ≪_ε T^{4+ε}. Your draft omits both the harmonic weight 1/L(1,ad f) and the exponent T^{4+ε}.
The moment is at the central point s=1/2, and the quantity being raised to the 12th power is L(1/2,f), not a t-aspect value L(1/2+it,f) and not a twisted central value.
To make the spectral parameter notation stand alone, one should define t_f by the Laplace eigenvalue 1/4+t_f^2.
The ambient automorphic setting should be stated explicitly: forms over Q, typically as Hecke–Maass cusp forms for Γ0(q).
"Bounded spectral parameter" should be made precise, e.g. 0 ≤ t_f ≤ T0 for a fixed cutoff T0 independent of q.

A stand-alone question should specify what family at level q is being summed over (for example, an orthonormal Hecke basis of the level-q cuspidal space); the paper itself does not say whether it intends the full level-q space or only newforms.
The adjoint factor should be identified: L(s,ad f) is the adjoint L-function of f, evaluated at s=1.
The quantifiers should be explicit: for every ε>0, with the implied constant allowed to depend on ε and on the fixed spectral cutoff.

If one wants a completely explicit level-aspect bound, the natural analogue for fixed spectral window is a q-aspect Weyl-strength estimate, but that exponent is not written out in the paper and must be unpacked from the phrase "level-aspect analogue."
refined_question: Fix T0>0. Let B_q(T0) be an orthonormal Hecke basis of Hecke–Maass cusp forms f of level q for Γ0(q) with trivial nebentypus, Laplace eigenvalue 1/4+t_f^2, and 0≤t_f≤T0, and let L(s,ad f) denote the adjoint L-function of f. Prove a level-aspect analogue of Jutila’s level-1 bound Σ_{t_f≤T} L(1/2,f)^12/L(1,ad f) ≪_ε T^{4+ε}, namely obtain the corresponding Weyl-strength twelfth-moment upper bound for Σ_{f∈B_q(T0)} L(1/2,f)^12/L(1,ad f) as q→∞ (naturally, one expects ≪_{T0,ε} q^{2+ε}).
justification: The paper is a problem list, so there is no relevant Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 for this draft; the nearest official formulation is exactly Problem (13). Your draft is already close to the paper’s wording, but it leaves out the displayed bound that defines what is being analogized: the central twelfth moment of L(1/2,f) weighted by 1/L(1,ad f) and bounded by T^{4+ε}. The rewrite restores those ingredients and makes the spectral cutoff and family precise enough to stand alone. The only mild interpretive step is spelling out what "level-aspect analogue" should mean in a fixed spectral window; the paper itself does not write the q-exponent explicitly, so the q^{2+ε} bound is included only as the natural unpacking of the paper’s wording, not as a separate official formulation.
